probes.explanation: REQ-6-1 counts only a reviewer's latest decision and states that any valid Request changes blocks merging; the merge area of a blocked PR must therefore offer no actionable merge control. Fixture: the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main with both toggles enabled, its current compare commit c-acme-3 carries a valid non-author approval (bob-reviewer) and test: success, and dana-dev — granted the minimal Write permission a reviewer needs — has one non-stale 'Changes requested' review on that same commit. The real merge-area renderer APP.pullSidebar derives eligibility from the approval count alone and never consults Request changes, so it emits an actionable Merge pull request button. Corrected from the failing version: the module-level escaping helper (var esc = ARC.esc) had no ARC.esc provided, so the renderer threw 'esc is not a function'; the fixture now supplies that escaping plumbing, which is external rendering plumbing, not the rule under test.

probes.requirement_text:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-4-3-1 (List and Switch Repository Branches) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. A “branch protection rule” is a persistent merge restriction bound to one exact branch name, displayed in the frontend under Settings → Branches, with the backend storing the branch name and rule toggles. This product supports only two independently selectable requirements: “at least 1 valid Approve from someone other than the PR author” and “required check `test` is success”. For a given reviewer on the same current compare commit, only the reviewer's latest decision among Comment, Approve, and Request changes counts. The PR author cannot satisfy the approval requirement; any valid Request changes blocks merging; when the compare branch gains a new commit, all decisions become stale and a new review is required. “Checks” is the results area on the PR detail page attached to the current compare commit; the `test` status of pending, success, or failure, together with the setter and time, must be stored, and only a repository Admin may update that status from this area. The system blocks direct writes to a protected branch and applies the rule during subsequent PR merging. The repository provides a Settings link followed by a Branches link. The rule form opens from the Add branch protection rule button and contains a field labeled Branch name pattern (an exact branch name, with no wildcard semantics), checkboxes named Require 1 approval and Require status check test, and a Create button; an existing rule uses Save changes. After saving and reloading, the branch name is visible verbatim with the summaries 1 approval and Require status check test. For a non-Admin, Add branch protection rule is absent, even if Settings or Branches remain accessible; rejecting a save alone is insufficient. On the PR detail page, the Checks area is available on arrival, displays test: pending initially, and offers the Admin a combobox named test status with a clickable option named success and a Save button. Saving displays test: success and identifies the setter and time, and reloading preserves the result for that compare commit. Seed data comprises a repository Admin and a readable non-Admin account, a dedicated repository and exact branch name with no existing rule before creation, and a separate Open PR targeting protected main with its current test check initially pending.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-branch-protection.png)

probes.explanation: REQ-6-5 requires that on a protected target each enabled rule is enforced independently, so an Open PR with a valid non-author approval but a `test` check that is not success stays blocked and shows a disabled Merge pull request button plus the unmet-condition explanation. Fixture: seeded PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main with both Require 1 approval and Require status check test enabled; bob-reviewer's approval is valid and non-stale for the current compare commit c-acme-3, no valid Request changes exists, and the check record for that same commit is 'pending'. APP.pullSidebar (the real merge-area renderer) computes ok from pr.status and the approval rule only and never reads the check rule, so it renders an actionable Merge pull request control for a PR that the protection rule requires to be blocked. Corrected from the failing version: ARC.esc (the external escaping plumbing consumed by the module-level esc helper) is now supplied in setup so the renderer can run.
probes.subject: pullSidebar
probes.requirement_text: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. Each seed state is restored independently before reuse. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

probes.explanation: REQ-6-3-3 requires that a draft started with Start a review stays pending: it is shown with 'Pending review' to its author but is not made public before review submission. Fixture: the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 is viewed by alice-dev (its author, a different account from the commenter bob-reviewer) and the Files changed store holds one already-published inline comment plus one unsubmitted (published:false) inline comment by bob-reviewer on the same current compare commit c-acme-3. APP.pullFiles, the real Files-changed renderer, lists every inline record of the PR without any author or publication check, so bob-reviewer's unsubmitted draft body is rendered to alice-dev and thus becomes public before submission. Corrected from the failing version: ARC.esc (the external escaping helper consumed by the module-level esc binding) is supplied in setup, and the fixture explicitly clears ui().lineEditor so the diff-line rendering path used here runs.
probes.subject: pullFiles
probes.requirement_text: An inline review comment is a comment record anchored to a file path, the current compare commit, and a specific added/deleted line in Files changed; it differs from an ordinary comment in Conversation that has no code location. A user with Write, Maintain, or Admin who is not the PR author can hover over a changed line, click the button visually shown as “+” and accessibly named Add comment, and choose “Add single comment” to publish immediately or “Start a review” to keep it as a pending review draft. The changed-line Add comment buttons are available for direct activation without a prerequisite hover; the first such button in document order targets the first commentable changed line. Activating one opens a single editor labeled Comment with Add single comment and Start a review buttons. Add single comment immediately displays the exact entered body in that diff view and retains it after reload. Start a review displays the body and Pending review to its author immediately, retains the pending draft after reload, and does not make it public before review submission. Seed data supplies a non-author Write reviewer, an Open reviewable PR with at least one changed line, and a separate Open PR for the pending-comment scenario. The system stores the PR, file path, compare commit, line position, author, body, and publication state; when the compare commit changes, published comments are retained but marked Outdated, while drafts are not published automatically. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-2 (Inspect Changed Files and Aggregate Diff) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.

probes.explanation: REQ-5-3-1 defines assignable members as accounts holding at least Triage permission on the current repository and states that non-assignable users do not appear in the results. In the seed, carol-reader is an organization member of acme-demo but holds only a direct Read grant on acme-docs (her only team is frontend-child, which has no grant and team hierarchy is not transitive), so the application's own predicate APP.canTriage(repo, carol-reader) is false, while bob-reviewer (direct Write) and the signed-in Owner are eligible. The picker renderer that the issue detail page is meant to show filters candidates by organization membership instead of repository permission, so it offers carol-reader as an assignable option. Corrected from the rejected version: the picker is declared inside the actions object, so it must be selected by its full declaration path APP.actions.assigneePicker (the runner reported APP.assigneePicker does not exist); ARC.esc and the ARC.route resolution used by the picker are supplied as external plumbing.
probes.subject: assigneePicker
probes.requirement_text: Only a signed-in user with Triage, Maintain, or Admin may click the settings icon in the “Assignees” area on the right side of an issue, search for and check assignable members, or uncheck selected members and close the menu. Matching assignee options update as the user types in the search textbox; pressing Enter or activating a separate search button is not required before selecting an option. Assignable members are accounts that have at least Triage permission on the current repository; the system stores the issue-account relationship, operator, and time and records an activity, while non-assignable users do not appear in results. The settings icon is a button named “Assignees”; the open selector contains a textbox named “Search assignees” and items with role option named exactly after the member username. Seed data provides an eligible member not initially assigned to the target issue. Clicking the member option immediately saves the assignment and closes the selector without a separate Save action; the exact username is visible in metadata and remains after reload. Reopening Assignees shows the selected member without requiring another search; clicking that option again immediately removes the assignment and closes the selector so the username is no longer displayed as an assignee. Historical assignment and unassignment activities remain historical records. Unassignment only deletes that issue relationship and does not delete the member account or repository grant; controls are unavailable to users without the role and the server rejects their submissions. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-5-1-2 (View an Issue and Its Discussion); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
